question.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ Every universal statement is not true.
question.worked_solution:
Let $U$ be the set of all universal statements. The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ For all $x\in U,$ $x$ is not true.

Introducing the universal quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∀x\in U,\,x\text{ is not true}.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀x\in U,\,x\text{ is not true}) & ≡∃x\in U,\,¬(x\text{ is not true}) \\  & ≡∃x\in U,\,x\text{ is true}\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ There exists $x\in U$ such that $x$ is true.

or simply

$\,$ Some universal statements are true.

choices.value: Some universal statements are not true.
All universal statements are not true.
